question: Walk me through the last Enterprise deal you lost at Propose or Negotiate — what actually happened first?
why: Stated exit criteria are aspirational; loss narratives expose the gate that actually existed (requirements-gathering Gotcha 10 / sales-process-mapping).
answer_shape: One rewritten exit criterion per stage where the current wording is aspirational, plus the field it makes required.
proposed_default: Today: one generic pipeline (the requirement states this); no stage-specific exit criteria exist yet for Enterprise deals, so no loss narrative is on file.

question: Who is allowed to move a deal into Negotiate, and who actually does today?
why: The platform allows backward and skipped stage moves silently — only a validation rule stops it.
answer_shape: The owner per stage transition, and either a validation-rule row or an explicit decision not to enforce stage order.

question: When an Enterprise or Renewal deal closes, who has to know, and what do they need from the record?
why: Closed Won exit obligations (onboarding case, contract, booking) get built by nobody unless they are named as stage requirements.
answer_shape: The Sales → Service and Sales → Finance handoff rows and the fields each needs; the requirement is silent on this.

question: Must the SMB team be unable to see Enterprise pipeline (and vice versa), or is this purely a process-guidance separation?
why: Record types and Sales Processes do not govern read access on their own — a visibility requirement routes to the sharing-selection decision tree instead.
answer_shape: A yes/no on cross-team visibility; if yes, a `sharing_impact` value naming the layer (OWD / role hierarchy / sharing rule / team) per standards/decision-trees/sharing-selection.md.
proposed_default: Not stated — requirement says only that the SMB process must not break, not that visibility must change.

question: Which forecast bucket does each of the six Enterprise stages and four Renewal stages belong in, and who signs off on that mapping?
why: ForecastCategoryName is per-stage and the forecast rolls up by category, not by stage; two stages in the same bucket collapse the distinction the ladder was built to create.
answer_shape: The stage-to-category table, which is the direct input to the StandardValueSet deploy.

question: What is the exact probability percentage for each of the six Enterprise stages and four Renewal stages?
why: The requirement asks for "a probability" per stage but states no values; without them the stage picklist cannot be deployed.
answer_shape: One probability value (0-100) per stage, agreed with the VP and the two managers.

question: Will Enterprise or Renewal opportunities ever use split credit, opportunity teams, or the Private flag?
why: Splits are a one-way door (split types cannot be deleted through any API) and IsPrivate silently removes teams, splits and sharing from a record — none of this is mentioned in the requirement.
answer_shape: An explicit yes/no per mechanism (splits, teams, IsPrivate), and a rule for who may set Private if it is ever allowed.
proposed_default: Not requested — the requirement describes only reps, two managers and a sales-ops admin with no mention of splits, teams or private opportunities.

question: Do Enterprise opportunities already exist on the generic record type that would need to be reassigned to the new Enterprise record type?
why: Reassignment blanks any picklist value absent from the target record type, silently, and existing StageName values on open deals may not exist in the new picklist.
answer_shape: The at-risk record count and the value-mapping step that must run before any reassignment.

question: Which reports, list views, or Flow entry criteria filter on the current single Opportunity record type today?
why: Report filters key on the label, which is not stable across a record-type change; code and Flows key on DeveloperName, which is.
answer_shape: The rename/reassignment blast-radius list before the existing generic record type is touched or retired.

question: How do Enterprise deals actually get closed — a rep in the UI, a manager doing a bulk edit, or a data load?
why: Close-path assumptions decide whether a validation rule is sufficient enforcement of the discount cap and product requirement.
answer_shape: The enforcement mechanism confirmed per rule rather than assumed by reflex.
proposed_default: Rep in the UI, one record at a time (12 reps, no integration and no migration per the requirement).

question: Of the "key fields per stage" the requirement asks for, which must be filled in before the rep can advance, versus merely shown for context?
why: Path displays; it does not enforce. The must-fill list is a validation-rule backlog, not a Path backlog, and the requirement does not separate the two.
answer_shape: A per-stage list split into must-fill (feeds admin/validation-rules) and shown-only fields.

question: Does the discount live on the Opportunity itself (a rollup or a header field) or only on the OpportunityLineItem records?
why: Validation rules don't fire on an Opportunity when only a child OpportunityLineItem changes; a rule guarding a header-level discount field never runs if the actual edit happens on the line item.
answer_shape: The object the discount field lives on, or a decision to use a record-triggered flow on OpportunityLineItem instead of (or alongside) an Opportunity-level validation rule.

question: Which users or integrations must be able to save an Enterprise/Renewal opportunity the product-count or discount-cap rule would otherwise reject?
why: Every rule with no bypass blocks every data load and every API write that does not meet the condition, including the sales-ops admin doing legitimate cleanup.
answer_shape: The Custom Permission name and the Permission Set that carries it, or a confirmed "no bypass" decision.
proposed_default: The sales-ops admin profile, via a Custom Permission bypass (per admin/validation-rules' own worked pattern) — no integration users, since the requirement states there are none.

question: Is the product-line field and the discount field confirmed to be on every layout, for every record type, that reps and managers use?
why: errorDisplayField silently changes to Top of Page when the field isn't visible on the layout the user is looking at, which reads as a confusing error location.
answer_shape: A confirmed layout placement per field per record type, or an error message rewritten to read correctly at the top of the page.

question: What should the two error messages say — the product-before-Propose rule and the 20%-discount-without-approval rule — in 255 characters or fewer each, naming both the problem and the fix?
why: errorMessage is capped at 255 characters; a rule that can't say what to do generates a support ticket per occurrence instead of a self-service fix.
answer_shape: The final message text for each rule, not a placeholder to be filled in at deploy time.

question: Do any open Enterprise opportunities today already violate the future product-count or discount-cap rules?
why: Validation rules fire on update as well as insert; an active rule on dirty data blocks every future edit of every violating record except the one edit that happens to satisfy the rule.
answer_shape: A decision to deploy the rule with active=false plus a named cleanup owner, or a count proving the existing pipeline is already clean.

question: What must NOT happen automatically here, and who fixes it when the validation rule or approval process is wrong for a specific deal?
why: "Enforce the discount cap" hides the exception path and the owner of the failure — every hard-blocking rule eventually meets a legitimate deal it should not have blocked.
answer_shape: The exception path and a named owner — most likely the sales-ops admin bypass already asked under admin/validation-rules — confirmed as complete for both the validation rule and the approval process.

question: Walk me through what a rep does today, end to end, when closing a deal with a discount above 20% — what do they type, where, and what happens next?
why: Stakeholders describe the workaround they built around the lack of a process as if it were the requirement; skipping this risks re-implementing today's ad hoc approval email chain rather than replacing it.
answer_shape: An As-Is step list tagged keep/drop/replace, confirming the new validation rule and approval process fully replace whatever ad hoc practice exists today.
proposed_default: Today: no formal cap or approval exists at all — the requirement states discounts above 20% are simply not stopped or approved today.

question: Which profile does each of the 12 reps, 2 managers and the sales-ops admin actually hold?
why: Permission sets grant record-type visibility only — the default record type and the page-layout assignment exist solely on Profile.
answer_shape: The profile x record-type x layout matrix for all 15 users, not a per-record-type layout list.

question: Which standard fields does the platform require on the Enterprise and Renewal Opportunity layouts?
why: A layout that omits a platform-required standard field does not deploy, and the required set is not documented in the Metadata API guide for Opportunity.
answer_shape: The layout-required item list confirmed before the layout XML is written, rather than one --dry-run round trip per missing field.

question: Is the stage picklist for each process final, or still being negotiated?
why: fieldName and recordTypeName on a PathAssistant are not updateable; re-pointing a Path after stages change is delete-and-recreate, not an edit.
answer_shape: A yes/no on whether the stage list is locked, and if not, a decision to build the Path after the stage model settles (admin/opportunity-management).

question: Is "discount" and "approval status" read from fields on Opportunity directly, or computed/rolled up from OpportunityLineItem?
why: The component's wire/imperative Apex call and its reactivity depend on which object and fields it reads; a field on the wrong object silently shows stale or blank data.
answer_shape: The exact field API names (object + field) the component reads for discount and for approval status.

question: Should an Enterprise opportunity with zero related products still appear on the open-pipeline report?
why: This decides outerJoin on the report type; an inner join makes those records invisible with no error and no empty row, which would hide exactly the deals the product-before-Propose rule is meant to catch early.
answer_shape: The report-type decision, and whether an existing Opportunity report type can be reused or a custom one is needed.
proposed_default: Yes, it should still appear — the report is meant to show open pipeline by stage, including deals that have not yet reached Propose.

question: Should the two managers each see only their own reps' opportunities on the report and dashboard, or the full Enterprise pipeline?
why: This is the dashboardType (SpecifiedUser vs LoggedInUser) decision; SpecifiedUser shows one person's data to everyone, LoggedInUser shows each viewer their own slice.
answer_shape: The running-user decision, and a named non-human service user if SpecifiedUser is chosen.

question: Who besides the two managers and the VP is allowed to see these rows, and who may open the report/dashboard folder?
why: Folder access and record access are separate layers; View on the folder only grants the right to run the report, not to see every row in it.
answer_shape: The folder accessType + folderShares design, and whether record-level sharing needs to change as well.
proposed_default: The two Enterprise managers, the VP, and the sales-ops admin; reps do not need folder access per the requirement ("Managers need a report...").

question: Is the Opportunity report type's exact API name (and the column codes for Stage, Amount and the discount field) confirmed from a retrieve against this org, rather than assumed?
why: Standard report type API names are not always the object name, and report column codes are report-type-specific; a plausible-looking guess is rejected only at deploy time with no offline way to confirm it.
answer_shape: The confirmed report-type API name and column codes as they appear in a retrieved report on this org, with an honest gap noted for anything that could not be harvested (this build is design-only, with no org connection to retrieve against).

question: Who may submit the approval request — the rep only, or also the sales-ops admin on the rep's behalf?
why: allowedSubmitters is required and typed (owner, creator, user, group, role, ...); leaving it at owner-only silently excludes anyone who submits on behalf of a rep. If the Apex invocable action calls setSubmitterId, that id must itself be in allowedSubmitters or the call is rejected.
answer_shape: The allowedSubmitters block, confirmed against who the requirement names as doing the submitting, and against the identity the Apex action will submit as.
proposed_default: The record owner (rep) and the two managers; the requirement does not mention the sales-ops admin submitting on a rep's behalf.

question: Should the rep be able to recall a submitted approval before the manager acts on it, and if so, is that admin-only or can the rep do it themselves?
why: Approval.process with action 'Removed' (recall) is admin-only in Apex; allowRecall=false on the process narrows recall to administrators entirely, which the LWC's button state needs to reflect.
answer_shape: A yes/no on rep-initiated recall, and if yes, the admin-context escalation the Apex action needs to perform it.

question: Does the invocable Apex action ever need to submit more than one opportunity at a time, or is it always exactly one record from the LWC button click?
why: Approval.process is DML with per-transaction limits (150 statements, 10,000 records); the invocable method's parameter shape (single vs List<Id>) and its bulk-safety design depend on the answer.
answer_shape: Confirmation of single-record invocation, or the chunking/bulk design if the action must ever be called for more than one record.
proposed_default: Exactly one record per invocation, triggered by a single button click on one opportunity's record page.

question: When Approval.process(req, false) returns a failed ProcessResult for a submission, what should the rep see, and does anyone besides the rep need to know?
why: allOrNone=false returns per-row ProcessResults that nothing reads unless the Apex action writes a handler for them; the LWC also needs a defined error shape to show the rep something more useful than a generic toast.
answer_shape: The error surface (an inline message on the LWC, a toast, or both) and whether a failed submission is logged or alerted anywhere beyond the rep's screen.

question: While an opportunity is pending approval, may the current approver (the manager) edit the record, or only an admin?
why: recordEditability is AdminOnly or AdminOrCurrentApprover; the record is locked otherwise, and the requirement says only "the opportunity is locked while pending" without naming who, if anyone, may still edit it.
answer_shape: The chosen enum value, and a named exception process for in-flight corrections if AdminOnly is chosen.
proposed_default: AdminOnly — the requirement's wording ("locked while pending") reads as a hard lock, with the sales-ops admin as the only exception path for corrections.

question: Who is the approver on each Enterprise/Renewal opportunity — the rep's direct manager via role/user hierarchy, or a fixed named approver?
why: Approver type is adhoc, user, userHierarchyField, relatedUserField, or queue; userHierarchyField only works if nextAutomatedApprover is declared, and a blank hierarchy field is a runtime submission failure, not a design-time error.
answer_shape: The approver type and source field, plus the fallback queue or validation rule for a rep with no manager set.
proposed_default: The rep's manager via the standard user role/manager hierarchy (2 managers named in the requirement), assuming the hierarchy field is populated for all 12 reps.

question: What should happen automatically on submit, approve, reject and recall — an email alert to the manager and the rep, a field update on an Approval_Status__c field the LWC reads, or both?
why: Approval actions are workflow action references (Alert, FieldUpdate, Task) that live in a separate workflow metadata file, not in the approval file; a referenced alert or field update that is missing fails the deploy, and the LWC's "approval status" display needs a field the approval process actually updates.
answer_shape: The action inventory per event (submit/approve/reject/recall), including the field the LWC will read for "approval status", and confirmation those actions exist before the approval process is built.

question: When the "Submit for approval" button is enabled — discount > 20% and not already pending/approved — should clicking it call an invocable Apex action that wraps Approval.process(), or should it navigate the rep to the standard Submit for Approval action?
why: Process.submit cannot be called directly from LWC; it requires an Apex invocable method, which is a distinct build artefact (its own class, its own test) from the component itself, and the requirement asks for a button embedded in a small custom component rather than a link to the standard action.
answer_shape: Confirmation of the mechanism (Apex invocable vs standard-action navigation) and, if Apex, the class name and its test plan.
proposed_default: An invocable Apex action wrapping Approval.process(), called imperatively from the LWC on button click, so the component can show a confirmation/error inline rather than navigating away.

question: How will the enable/disable logic for the Submit button be tested — what Jest stubs and what Apex test class are expected as acceptance evidence?
why: The sfdx-lwc-jest lightning-stubs fire no events and do not reflect every property as a DOM attribute; a test asserting getAttribute() on the button's disabled state can pass for the wrong reason.
answer_shape: A test plan naming the properties set/read on the stub and the events dispatched, plus the Apex test class covering the invocable action's bulk and negative-path behaviour.

question: Do Enterprise and Renewal run genuinely different stage sequences, confirming two Sales Processes are needed?
why: Two sequences means two Sales Processes, and businessProcess is required on an Opportunity record type.
answer_shape: Confirmation plus the record-type count, which is the largest cost line in the handoff brief.
proposed_default: Yes — the requirement names two distinct stage lists (Qualify..Closed Lost vs Renewal Review..Closed Lost), so two Sales Processes and two Record Types are required.

question: What does the board pack call each forecast bucket for Enterprise and Renewal deals?
why: Only the documented ForecastCategoryName values exist as platform values; a mismatched internal label creates a silent forecast-rollup gap.
answer_shape: The internal-label to platform-value translation table, or a decision to hold a separate forecast session.
proposed_default: Standard ForecastCategoryName values (Pipeline, Best Case, Commit, Closed) mapped one-to-one to the stages named in the requirement, pending sign-off.

question: Does any integration or Apex write Probability or ForecastCategoryName directly on an Enterprise or Renewal opportunity?
why: Both fields are overridable per record, and a StageName update in the same transaction silently overwrites the override.
answer_shape: A confirmed empty list of writers, or the list to fix before the ladder ships.
proposed_default: No — the requirement states no integrations exist or are being added.

question: How will Enterprise/Renewal stage movement be measured six months from now?
why: Stage history cannot be backfilled, and OpportunityHistory is not itself a stage-history table.
answer_shape: Confirmation that history tracking is switched on at deploy time, and the report/query chosen up front.
proposed_default: Field history tracking enabled on StageName from day one; reporting uses OpportunityFieldHistory / OpportunityHistory as appropriate.

question: Which picklist values differ between the Enterprise and Renewal processes, field by field, beyond StageName?
why: If nothing else differs, a second record type is warranted purely by StageName/businessProcess, which the requirement already implies; if something else differs, that becomes an additional picklistValues block.
answer_shape: The full picklistValues block per record type, and confirmation no other field needs to differ.
proposed_default: StageName is confirmed to differ (from the requirement); no other differing picklist is named.

question: Are Person Accounts enabled on this org?
why: Person Account record types are a separate model and the Metadata API will not round-trip their custom picklist values; this changes the record-type build.
answer_shape: A confirmed no, or a separate design track and manual verification step if yes.
proposed_default: No — the requirement describes an Enterprise B2B sales process with no mention of Person Accounts.

question: Is the "at least one product line before Propose" rule meant to be enforced everywhere (API, every layout, Flow), or only on the standard UI?
why: Layout Required binds to that layout only — API, Flow and every other layout ignore it, so a layout-level control alone would not meet the requirement's wording.
answer_shape: Confirmation that this is a validation-rule decision, not a layout-required decision.
proposed_default: Enforced everywhere via a validation rule, not a layout-Required setting, since the requirement says the opportunity "cannot move to Propose" without qualification.

question: Is any workflow field update or other legacy automation writing to StageName, Amount or the discount field after save on Enterprise/Renewal opportunities?
why: Custom validation rules are not re-run after a workflow field update re-saves the record, so the rule would not be a database invariant if one exists.
answer_shape: Either a migration of any such field update to a before-save flow, or an explicit acceptance that violating records can exist.
proposed_default: No — the requirement describes a net-new process with no existing automation named on these fields.

question: Does the discount-cap formula need to read a compound field, a person name, or a dependent picklist?
why: Validation rules cannot use compound fields as of API version 20.0.
answer_shape: Confirmation the formula only touches simple number/picklist fields, or the component-field rewrite if not.
proposed_default: No — discount is expected to be a plain percent/number field on Opportunity or OpportunityLineItem.

question: Will the discount-cap or product-count formula need to test a picklist field (e.g. an approval-status picklist) with ISBLANK or ISNULL?
why: The org rejects ISBLANK()/ISNULL() called directly on a picklist field at deploy time; only TEXT(<picklist>) is accepted inside those functions.
answer_shape: Confirmation of which fields the formula reads and that any picklist reads go through TEXT().
proposed_default: Likely yes, if approval status is read as a picklist in the formula — NOT(ISBLANK(TEXT(Field__c))) will be used rather than the direct form.

question: Does each of the two record types (Enterprise, Renewal) need its own Path, or does the same guidance serve both?
why: Exactly one Path can exist per record type per object, including __Master__ — record type is the only differentiator available.
answer_shape: The file count: one .pathAssistant-meta.xml per record type, each with a named owner.
proposed_default: Two Paths, one per record type, since the two processes have different stage lists per the requirement.

question: Which edition is the target org (including any sandboxes/scratch orgs used to build this)?
why: pathAssistantEnabled defaults to true only in Enterprise Edition; a Path deploys fine into an org where Path is off and simply never renders.
answer_shape: Confirmation of edition, and settings/PathAssistant.settings-meta.xml included in the package instead of a manual per-org Setup step.
proposed_default: Sales Cloud Enterprise, per the requirement — pathAssistantEnabled should default on, but the settings file should still ship to make it explicit.

question: Does anyone need to see the Path guidance without clicking to expand it?
why: The Path loads collapsed unless canOverrideAutoPathCollapseWithUserPref is true (default false in every edition).
answer_shape: A decision on the org-wide expand preference before rep adoption of the checklist is measured.

question: Who advances the stage — the rep in the UI, or automation?
why: Celebration is a UI interaction reward and has no element in PathAssistant metadata at all, so it never travels with a deploy if the rep never clicks Mark Stage as Complete.
answer_shape: Either a celebration stage the rep actually clicks through, or an honest "no celebration" decision.
proposed_default: The rep in the UI, since the requirement describes reps working the pipeline manually with no mention of stage-advancing automation.

question: Which Lightning record page will render the Path and the new discount/approval LWC together?
why: The Path component is runtime_sales_pathassistant:pathAssistant in the subheader region; a page template without that region has nowhere to put it, and the requirement asks for both Path and the LWC on the same record page.
answer_shape: The named FlexiPage that must ship in the same package as the Path and the LWC.
proposed_default: The existing Enterprise Opportunity Lightning record page (or a new one cloned from it), confirmed to include the subheader region.

question: Does the discount/approval component need to run anywhere besides the standard Lightning Experience record page (mobile app, an Experience Cloud site)?
why: Container decides half the component list — lightning-datatable/tree-grid are unsupported on mobile, and only a subset of base components server-side render on an LWR site.
answer_shape: The supportedFormFactors block for the .js-meta.xml.
proposed_default: Lightning Experience desktop and the Salesforce mobile app only — the requirement describes reps and managers on the record page, with no Experience Cloud mention.

question: Is the discount value ever edited inline in this component, or only ever displayed?
why: lightning-output-field is read-only and must be a direct child of lightning-record-view-form; an editable field needs a different component shape entirely (lightning-record-edit-form or lightning-input-field).
answer_shape: Confirmation the component is read-only apart from the Submit button.
proposed_default: Displayed only — the requirement describes the component showing discount, approval status and a button, not an edit surface.

question: Will anyone email, export, or subscribe to the open-pipeline report or the dashboard tile?
why: Subscriptions send the running user's rows to every recipient, which interacts with the dashboardType decision above.
answer_shape: A go/no-go on subscriptions for the two managers and the VP.

question: Does the existing custom report type (if the pipeline report reuses one from the SMB process) already back other reports?
why: Editing a shared custom report type reaches every report built on it; removing or adding a column removes/adds it everywhere that report type is used, which is exactly the "don't break SMB" risk named in the requirement.
answer_shape: A blast-radius check before any existing report type is touched, or confirmation a new one is being created instead.
proposed_default: Unknown — assume a new, Enterprise-scoped report type is built rather than editing whatever the SMB report type is, to protect the "nothing should break SMB" requirement.

question: Is the dashboard tile's "pipeline by close month" component going to be filtered by anything else on the dashboard (e.g. by owner or by record type)?
why: A dashboard component only responds to a dashboard filter if it declares dashboardFilterColumns for that field.
answer_shape: The filter design and per-component column mapping if a filter is wanted after all.
proposed_default: No additional filter beyond the tile itself, per the requirement's plain "dashboard tile of the pipeline by close month."

question: Does "pipeline by close month" need historical trending (how the pipeline looked a month ago), or only the current snapshot?
why: Historical trending only starts collecting data the day it is enabled; there is no retroactive data.
answer_shape: Either a trend design started now (accepting a forward-only data start), or confirmation the snapshot view is sufficient.
proposed_default: Current snapshot only — the requirement asks for a dashboard tile of the pipeline by close month, not a trend-over-time view.

question: For the open-pipeline report, what exact number does the VP need, and what has to appear on the same row as it?
why: Reporting requirements assume joins the report-type rules forbid; a four-object join chain is the ceiling.
answer_shape: A reporting row naming base object (Opportunity), join chain (none beyond OpportunityLineItem if discount lives there), and whether rows with no product line must still appear.
proposed_default: Amount and discount on the same row as Stage and Opportunity Name, per the requirement's "report of open Enterprise opportunities by stage with amount and discount."

question: Will Enterprise Opportunity ever need more than this one approval process (e.g. a separate one for Renewal, or a future contract-terms approval)?
why: A submission enters exactly one process; entry criteria are evaluated in the org's process order, and process order is not carried in the metadata, so a second process later becomes a manual re-ordering step in every org.
answer_shape: The ordered process list (today: one process) plus a note that order must be re-set by hand in the target org after deploy if a second process is added later.
proposed_default: One process, entry criteria "Discount > 20%", used by both Enterprise and Renewal opportunities per the requirement.

question: Will this approval process ever have more than one approver on a single step (needing whenMultipleApprovers), or is it always exactly one manager?
why: On a unanimous multi-approver step, one rejection flips every other approver's StepStatus to NoResponse rather than Rejected, which changes what the LWC's approval-status field should show.
answer_shape: Confirmation of single-approver-per-step, or the whenMultipleApprovers value and the status-field mapping if not.
proposed_default: Exactly one approver per step — the requirement names a single manager approval, not a panel.

question: If a manager rejects the approval, does the request die entirely, or can the rep resubmit after adjusting the discount?
why: rejectBehavior (RejectRequest vs BackToPrevious) is set per step and cannot be changed once the process has been activated, even after deactivating it.
answer_shape: The per-step reject behaviour, decided before the first activation, and confirmation the rep can simply resubmit a corrected request afterward.
proposed_default: RejectRequest — a single-step process (rep to manager) has no prior step to return to.

question: Should an opportunity that does not actually need approval (discount ≤ 20%) be auto-approved if it is ever routed into this process by mistake, or should it never enter the process at all?
why: ifCriteriaNotMet is ApproveRecord, RejectRecord (first step only), or GotoNextStep; the entry criteria should mean this never happens, but the field still has to be set.
answer_shape: Confirmation entry criteria are the real gate, with the field set defensively.
proposed_default: The process entry criteria (Discount > 20%) should prevent this; the field itself is not user-facing so any legal value is acceptable — default ApproveRecord.

question: How many Enterprise/Renewal opportunities are created a day, and what is the biggest single batch anyone would ever push through this process?
why: Automation that passes UAT on ten records fails on a large batch; this decides whether the validation rule and approval process need to consider bulk/API entry paths at all.
answer_shape: A data_volume value with a steady-state number and a worst-case batch number.
proposed_default: Very low volume and single-record entry — 12 reps, no integration, no data migration, per the requirement.

question: When you say managers need to see the report — can reps not open it at all, or can they open it but should the discount/amount not be visible to them?
why: Record access and field access are different mechanisms configured in different places, and "record access" itself is seven ordered layers.
answer_shape: A sharing_impact value naming the layer (folder access here) plus a separate FLS row if field-level hiding is also wanted.
proposed_default: Reps cannot open the report/dashboard folder at all, per the requirement's "Managers need a report..." wording; no field-level discount hiding is implied.

question: Who exactly works this process — Northwind employees only, or does any partner or customer-facing portal user touch an Enterprise/Renewal opportunity?
why: The answer selects a licence, and licence selects API allocation, object access and portal template long before design starts.
answer_shape: A licence_implication value confirming standard Salesforce (internal) licences throughout.
proposed_default: Employees only — 12 reps, 2 managers, 1 sales-ops admin, all named as internal roles in the requirement.

question: Where does the discount value and the product-line data live right now — only in Salesforce, or does it originate in a quoting tool or spreadsheet?
why: A requirement sourced from another system is an integration requirement wearing a validation-rule costume, and needs a pattern decision before sizing.
answer_shape: Confirmation of "Salesforce only," closing off the integration-pattern-selection branch for this build.
proposed_default: Salesforce only — the requirement explicitly states no integrations and no data migration.
